newsitem.title: UK: Moss Bros to offer four one share bonus.
newsitem.headline: Moss Bros to offer four one share bonus.

text.p: British clothing retailer Moss Bros Group said on Monday that it was planning to offer a bonus of four shares for one share held by each shareholder.
The company's managing director Rowland Gee told Reuters that the bonus would be offered out of its share premium account which has about eight million stg.

"The aim is to reduce the spread and improve marketability (of shares)," Gee said after the company reported a 41 percent rise in its pre-tax profits to 15.92 million stg for the year to January, 1997.
He said the company's brands had achieved a three percent share in the overall retail clothing market while a 10 percent share has been achieved in the suit segment.
The group said it hoped to open eight more sites in addition to its existing 164 shops. Moss Bros had opened 13 shops in 1996/97.
The company's trading in the current year has so far been in line with its expectations with like-for-like sales rising 7.50 percent in the first eight weeks since February.
The company plans to make a capital expenditure of about 10 million stg this year for refurbishing some of its shops, Gee said.
